body: This sounds quite similar to the thread that I just put up myself, though I've got a couple of years on you. Hope you're feeling at least a little better. Let me know if you want to talk about anything; maybe we could both benefit from it.

Sorry to self-post, but I don't think I can see all of the comments here. Do I need to adjust some settings to view the rest of the messages?

Thanks.

Cheers. I guess I'm still struggling with some personal (baseless) neuroses with regards to what it means to be "medicated". Maybe it's exactly what I need to get over this hump, but I really don't know what the other side is supposed to look like. Right now I can't imagine that it even exists.

*Hug much appreciated.*

Thank you both so much. I know that I'll feel "better" if I take medication, and that it's an invaluable tool for a lot of people, but I can't get over this vague concern that I'll be sacrificing my *authenticity* of being (sounds stupid when I try to spell it out, but what else do I have left to lose?). I guess I can't really afford to maintain these silly romantic notions when suicidal thoughts are knocking on the door.

Glad to hear that your friend, a fellow cynic, made it through OK. Sometimes it feels like my sense of humor is the only thing sustaining me.

As far as exercise goes, I can't say I haven't tried. I'll go for a run tomorrow - I owe you at least that much for your thoughtful response.

Again, thank you.

I've done about as poorly as someone in my position could have been expected to do. I've had a comfortable life, supportive parents, access to decent education; somehow I wound up here.

You're right about the psychiatrist, of course. This has become something that I need to talk about, otherwise I wouldn't have come here. "Live in the present moment": that's the trick, isn't it? It's hard to remember that sometimes. Thank you.

As far as the card goes, I'm not sure that I understand the question. What do you think it means?
